links.outcome: Perceived documentation time, after-hours work, cognitive workload, and objective EHR documentation minutes after ambient scribe pilot
links.effect: Perceived documentation time and after-hours work fell significantly (all p < 0.001, r = 0.73-0.80); NASA-TLX domains decreased (g = 0.76-1.54); objective EHR documentation minutes did not change (t(15) = 1.52, p = 0.15, g = 0.36).
links.quote: These findings suggest that ambient AI scribes meaningfully reduce perceived workload and improve calibration of documentation burden, even when measurable documentation time remains stable.

screen.reason: Prospective pre-post pilot evaluating the real-world deployment of an ambient AI scribe tool on clinician cognitive workload, burnout, and EHR documentation time.
